verses.1: A psalm for Asaph. God, the God of the LORD, has spoken and summoned the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
verses.2: From Zion, the beauty of his splendor has shone forth.
verses.3: Our God comes; he will not be silent. Fire devours before him, and around him a storm rages mightily.
verses.4: He calls to the heavens above and to the earth to judge his people.
verses.5: Gather to me my righteous ones, those who made my covenant, who offer sacrifices to me.
verses.6: And the heavens will declare his righteousness, for God is a judge. Selah.
verses.7: Listen, my people, and I will speak. Israel, and I will bear witness against you: I am the God who is your God.
verses.8: I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are ever before me.
verses.9: I will not take a bull from your house, nor a ram from your folds.
verses.10: For all the beasts of the forest are mine, the cattle on a thousand mountains.
verses.11: I know every bird of the heavens, and the wild animals of the field are with me.
verses.12: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and all in it are mine.
verses.13: Do I eat the flesh of mighty bulls, or drink the blood of the rams?
verses.14: Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
verses.15: And when you call to me in the day of trouble, I will deliver you, and you will honor me.
verses.16: But to the wicked God says: What right do you have to recite my statutes, to take my covenant on your lips?
verses.17: You have hated instruction and cast my words behind your back.
verses.18: If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you shared the portion of the adulterers.
verses.19: Your mouth was filled with evil, and your tongue wove deceit.
verses.20: You sat in ambush with your brother, you slandered the son of your mother.
verses.21: These things you did and I was silent. You thought I was just like you, but I will confront you and set your sins before you.
verses.22: Understand this, you who forget God, or else I will tear you apart, with no one to save you.
verses.23: One who offers a sacrifice of praise honors me, and to the one who plans his way I will show the salvation of God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The phrase "God, the God of the LORD" reflects the Hebrew's dual use of el and YHWH, emphasizing the deity's supreme identity.
- v. 6: The placement of "Selah" at the end of this verse is conventional and reflects the poetic structure of the psalm.
- v. 12–13: The rhetorical questions in v. 13 are rendered as statements to preserve the tone of divine irony and self-declaration.
- v. 23: "Plans his way" translates the Hebrew "שָׂם דֶּרֶךְ," which may be interpreted either as "sets a path" or "plans a course," depending on the context.
